statement: Micron's unionized Taiwan workforce is moving toward a strike over bonus terms, with around 80% of unionized workers backing labor action; Taiwan hosts roughly 60% of Micron's global production capacity, mandatory mediation is expected to begin mid-September 2026, and a formal strike vote becomes possible in September 2026 if talks fail.
why: Micron is a major DRAM and HBM supplier; a work stoppage at sites representing roughly 60% of its global capacity would tighten memory availability for AI accelerator builds.

impact.mechanism: A strike or slowdown at Micron's Taiwan fabs would cut memory output, and HBM/DRAM supply is already the binding constraint on GPU system shipments.

evidence.excerpt: around 80% of unionized workers support labor action
Taiwan hosts roughly 60% of Micron's global production capacity.
mandatory mediation expected to begin mid-September 2026; if talks fail, a formal strike vote becomes possible in September 2026.

confidence.basis: Single secondary outlet (BigGo Finance) with specific survey and timeline detail; no strike has occurred and no company or union filing confirms the vote share.
